title: Orcas hunt with a wave

scenes.headline: These orcas hunt with a wave.
Step 1: spot the seal
scenes.body: Pack-ice orcas lift their heads out of the water to scan the floes for resting seals.

scenes.headline: Step 2: charge side by side
scenes.body: Swimming fast in a line, their tail strokes push up a wave that washes the seal off the ice.

scenes.label: seal attacks used the wave trick
scenes.body: Pack-ice orcas off the Antarctic Peninsula, NOAA study.

scenes.headline: Teamwork, not brute force.
scenes.body: Orcas are the largest members of the dolphin family.

caption:
Orcas don't always chase seals. Sometimes they make a wave.

Researchers watched pack-ice orcas pick out Weddell seals almost every time, even though they were only about 15% of the seals around them.

Source: Pitman & Durban 2012, Marine Mammal Science; NOAA Fisheries. Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Predation done as hunting strategy only (no contact, no blood) from two CC photos of one real hunt. HIGH-RISK format: 'nature is metal' reels are almost always third-party kill clips; the real series is only OK with our own footage.
